newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican volcano spews ash after period of calm.
newsitem.headline: Mexican volcano spews ash after period of calm.

text.p: The Mexican volcano Popocatepetl spewed gases, vapour and ash on Wednesday in the first notable activity since a June 30 eruption forced the closure of the Mexico City airport, officials said.
The majestic, snow-capped volcano known simply as "Popo" is 33 miles (50 km) southeast of Mexico City.
A cloud of vapour and ash from the volcano reached a little over a mile (about 2 km) into the sky and was visible from the capital.
"It's really a small exhalation compared to the one on June 30, but it is the first one since then," Berta Lopez, a data analyst with the National Centre for the Prevention of Disaster, told Reuters.
A month ago, the volanco sent a cloud of ash and acrid gases over greater Mexico City, causing eyes and throat irritation to some of the area's 18 million people.
The ash was so thick then that authorities were forced to close the Mexico City airport, and motorists needed windscreen wipers to see clearly.
